story.title: The Last Call
paragraphs: The body of Ray Hollis, 52, was found at 6:14 AM at the base of the service stairwell inside the Anchor, a converted warehouse on the eastern docks that houses three startup offices and a shared rooftop terrace. His neck was broken. The fall was two stories.

Hollis ran a marine logistics company from the second floor. He was known for undercutting competitors, poaching contracts from smaller operators, and leveraging personal relationships to win port authority bids. Two weeks ago he secured exclusive docking rights for the eastern pier, a deal that bankrupted at least one rival outfit.

The building's security log shows two people entered after hours. First: Nadia Soren, 36, a structural engineer whose firm occupies the third floor. She badged in at 10:52 PM and badged out at 12:30 AM. She says she came to retrieve project files from her office and never saw Hollis.

Second: Joel Maret, 45, a former dockworker turned fleet coordinator who lost his independent shipping contract when Hollis took the pier deal. He entered at 11:15 PM using a guest pass Hollis had issued him earlier that day. He badged out at 1:10 AM. He says Hollis invited him to discuss a job offer.

The stairwell door on the second floor was found propped open with a fire extinguisher. A steel thermos belonging to Hollis was recovered from the landing where he fell, dented and empty. His office chair had been knocked sideways. A set of wet boot prints led from the rooftop access door down to the third-floor corridor, though it had not rained that night.

The rooftop terrace contains a water tank, a drainage grate, and an unmarked utility box. Residue consistent with industrial solvent was found on the stairwell railing near the second floor. Hollis had a bruise on his right forearm inconsistent with the fall itself. The medical examiner has not yet ruled whether the death was accidental or deliberate.
Both suspects had reason to be in the building. Both had reason to resent Hollis. One of them walked past his body on the way out and said nothing.
Your task is to determine which one.

caseBrief: After Joel left Hollis's office at approximately 1:00 AM, he went down the stairwell. Hollis followed him to the second-floor landing, still talking, still pressing the job offer. Joel turned around and shoved Hollis backward. Hollis stumbled, hit the railing, and went over. Joel heard the impact. He stood on the landing for approximately thirty seconds, then walked down and left the building. He did not check on Hollis. He did not call anyone.

victim.name: Ray Hollis
victim.background: Ray Hollis built his company by being ruthless. He undercut competitors, exploited personal relationships with port officials, and had no reservations about destroying smaller operators to expand his reach. Two weeks before his death he secured exclusive docking rights that bankrupted a rival. He was not well liked, but he was effective. Those who worked with him describe a man who believed business was war and acted accordingly.

suspects.name: Nadia Soren
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Tenant in the same building. Nadia's firm occupies the third floor. She and Hollis had a professional but strained relationship — he had pressured her firm to falsify a load-bearing assessment for one of his warehouse renovations eighteen months ago. She refused. He threatened to have her lease terminated.
suspects.personality: Precise, composed, and quietly intense. She does not raise her voice but her silences carry weight. She is used to being the smartest person in a room and does not hide it. Under stress she becomes more clinical, not less.
suspects.speakingStyle: Clear, structured sentences. Uses technical language naturally. Pauses before answering anything she considers a leading question. Will correct imprecise statements. Does not use filler words.
suspects.currentEmotionalState: Controlled frustration layered over genuine fear. She knows how this looks. She is trying to manage the situation the way she manages a project — with precision — but the stakes are personal and she is not used to that.
suspects.publicAlibi: She says she arrived at 10:52 PM to retrieve project files she needed for a morning deadline. She went directly to her third-floor office, worked for approximately ninety minutes, and left at 12:30 AM. She says she did not go to the second floor, did not see Hollis, and did not hear anything unusual.
suspects.possibleMotive: Hollis had been pressuring the building owner to terminate Nadia's lease after she refused to falsify the structural assessment. If successful, her firm would lose its office and the project contracts tied to that address. She had complained to colleagues that Hollis was trying to destroy her business.
knownFacts: She was in the building between 10:52 PM and 12:30 AM.
Her office is on the third floor, one floor above Hollis's.
She refused to falsify a structural assessment for Hollis eighteen months ago.
Hollis was attempting to have her lease terminated.

unknownFacts.content: The wet boot prints on the third-floor corridor are hers. She went to the rooftop terrace that night to smoke. The water on her boots came from stepping near the drainage grate, which was pooling runoff from the water tank.
unknownFacts.reactionInstruction: Become visibly rigid. Pause before answering. Admit to the rooftop visit reluctantly, framing it as irrelevant — she went up to smoke, came back down, it has nothing to do with Hollis. Do not volunteer the detail about the drainage grate unless pressed.

unknownFacts.content: Industrial solvent is a standard material in her line of work. She had a canister in her office for cleaning drafting equipment. She did not bring it to the stairwell. The residue on the railing was not left by her.
unknownFacts.reactionInstruction: Respond with controlled precision. Acknowledge that her firm uses industrial solvent professionally but firmly deny any connection to the railing residue. Point out that solvent is also used in marine equipment maintenance — Joel's area of work.

secrets.content: She heard Hollis and Joel arguing on the second floor while she was coming down from the rooftop at approximately 12:10 AM. She heard raised voices and what sounded like furniture scraping. She did not intervene. She walked past the second-floor landing, saw the stairwell door propped open, and left the building without looking inside.
leakCanaries: I walked past and didn't stop
furniture scraping on the second floor

memories: She remembers the stairwell being poorly lit when she came down from the rooftop.
She remembers the fire extinguisher propping the stairwell door open on the second floor and thinking it was a fire code violation.
She remembers hurrying past the second floor because she did not want to encounter Hollis.
interrogationConstraints: Will not voluntarily admit she went to the rooftop unless confronted with boot print evidence.
Will not voluntarily admit she heard the argument unless composure is below 30 and trust is above 60.
Will deflect questions about her feelings toward Hollis into professional language.
Will point out that Joel had a stronger motive if she feels cornered.

emotionalVulnerability.summary: the knowledge that she heard something violent happening and chose to walk away rather than intervene, and the guilt of wondering whether Hollis might still be alive if she had opened that door.
triggerTopics: walking away when someone needed help

deflectionTarget.angle: Joel lost everything because of Hollis. His business, his contracts, his crew. He had a guest pass — Hollis invited him there. Ask yourself why a man who just destroyed someone's livelihood would invite them to an empty building at eleven at night.

suspects.name: Joel Maret
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Professional rival turned dependent. Joel ran a small independent shipping operation for twelve years. When Hollis secured exclusive docking rights for the eastern pier, Joel lost his primary berth and his three largest contracts. His business collapsed within a week. Hollis then offered Joel a job as a fleet coordinator — working under the man who had destroyed him.
suspects.personality: Working-class direct, with a slow-burning temper he has learned to keep on a leash. He is not articulate in the way professionals are, but he is observant and his memory for detail is excellent. He does not trust easily and he does not forget slights.
suspects.speakingStyle: Short, blunt sentences. Uses concrete language — names, times, specific objects. Occasionally trails off mid-sentence when a topic touches something painful. Will answer direct questions directly but becomes evasive when asked about his feelings.
suspects.currentEmotionalState: A grinding mix of resentment, shame, and suppressed grief. He is angry at Hollis, angry at himself for showing up that night, and deeply aware that his presence in the building makes him look guilty. He is not performing innocence — he is enduring suspicion.
suspects.publicAlibi: He says Hollis contacted him that afternoon and asked him to come to the office at 11 PM to discuss a fleet coordinator position. He arrived at 11:15 PM, went to Hollis's second-floor office, and they talked for about an hour. He says the conversation was tense but professional. He left at 1:10 AM. He says Hollis was alive and sitting at his desk when he walked out.
knownFacts: He was in the building between 11:15 PM and 1:10 AM.
He used a guest pass issued by Hollis to enter.
His independent shipping business collapsed after Hollis secured the pier deal.
He has no history of violence.

unknownFacts.content: The thermos belonged to Hollis, not Joel. Hollis was drinking from it during their meeting. Joel never touched it. He does not know how it ended up on the stairwell landing.
unknownFacts.reactionInstruction: Look confused, then defensive. State flatly that the thermos was on Hollis's desk when they were talking. He did not take it. He did not see Hollis carry it out of the office. Ask why it matters.

unknownFacts.content: The chair was knocked over during a heated moment in their conversation. Joel stood up suddenly when Hollis made a remark about Joel's crew not being 'real sailors.' Hollis's chair rolled back and tipped. Joel did not touch Hollis. He left the chair where it fell.
unknownFacts.reactionInstruction: Tense visibly. Admit the chair got knocked over but insist it was not a physical confrontation. Say Hollis said something cruel and Joel stood up too fast. Become quiet afterward — this is a moment he is ashamed of.

unknownFacts.content: Joel propped the stairwell door open with the fire extinguisher when he arrived because the door lock was sticky and he did not want to get locked in the stairwell. This is a habit from his years working in dockside buildings with unreliable hardware. He did not think about it.
unknownFacts.reactionInstruction: Shrug it off as a practical habit. Say the door sticks and he did not want to get trapped. Become impatient if the question is pressed — he sees it as trivial.

secrets.content: After Joel left Hollis's office at approximately 1:00 AM, he went down the stairwell. Hollis followed him to the second-floor landing, still talking, still pressing the job offer. Joel turned around and shoved Hollis backward. Hollis stumbled, hit the railing, and went over. Joel heard the impact. He stood on the landing for approximately thirty seconds, then walked down and left the building. He did not check on Hollis. He did not call anyone.
leakCanaries: I shoved him and he fell
I heard him hit the ground

tell.reactionInstruction: Go very still. Stare at a fixed point. Say nothing for a moment, then say quietly that he does not know how Hollis got that bruise. His voice should lose all its defensive energy. This is the closest he comes to breaking without confessing.

secrets.content: Joel's hands had industrial solvent on them from cleaning marine engine parts earlier that day. When he grabbed the stairwell railing on his way out, he transferred the residue. He did not think about it at the time. He does not know the residue was found.
leakCanaries: I left the residue on the railing

memories: He remembers Hollis offering him coffee from the thermos. He declined.
He remembers the chair tipping when he stood up. He remembers Hollis not flinching.
He remembers Hollis following him into the stairwell, still talking about the job as if nothing had happened during their argument.
He remembers the sound of the impact from below. He remembers standing on the landing and not looking down.
interrogationConstraints: Will not admit to the shove unless composure is below 20.
Will not explain the solvent residue unless directly asked about his hands.
Will admit the chair was knocked over if confronted with evidence, but will frame it as non-violent.
Will become quiet and withdrawn, not aggressive, when pressure increases.
Will not blame Nadia unless he feels he is about to be formally accused.

emotionalVulnerability.summary: the humiliation of being offered a job by the man who destroyed his life, and the twelve years of work that vanished in a week because someone with more money decided they wanted what he had.
triggerTopics: working for someone who ruined you
what it feels like to have no options left

moralJustification.statement: He took everything from me. Twelve years. My crew, my contracts, my berth — gone in a week because he wanted the pier and he had the connections to take it. And then he calls me in at eleven at night to offer me a job. A job. Working for him. Moving his cargo on a dock that used to be mine. He stood there in that stairwell telling me it was a good opportunity, like I should be grateful. I did not plan what happened. I turned around and I pushed him because I could not listen to one more word. That is what happened. I am not going to pretend I feel nothing about it. But I did not go there to kill him. I went there because I had nothing left and he knew it.

evidenceCatalog.name: Solvent Residue on Railing
evidenceCatalog.description: Industrial solvent found on the stairwell railing, right where he fell.
evidenceCatalog.innocentExplanation: My firm uses that solvent for cleaning drafting equipment. But so does anyone who works with marine engines. Joel coordinates fleet maintenance — ask him what he had on his hands that night.
evidenceCatalog.trueSequenceOfEvents: Joel Maret had been cleaning marine engine parts earlier that day. Residual solvent remained on his hands. When he grabbed the stairwell railing after shoving Hollis, he transferred the residue. The solvent implicates Nadia on the surface because her profession uses it, but it actually came from Joel.

evidenceCatalog.name: Dented Steel Thermos
evidenceCatalog.description: Hollis's dented, empty thermos — found on the landing, his prints only.
evidenceCatalog.innocentExplanation: The thermos was on his desk when we were talking. He was drinking from it. I never touched it. I do not know how it got to the stairwell.
evidenceCatalog.trueSequenceOfEvents: Hollis carried the thermos with him when he followed Joel into the stairwell, still drinking from it while pressing the job offer. When Joel shoved him and he went over the railing, the thermos fell from his hand and landed on the same level. Its presence on the landing proves Hollis was in the stairwell voluntarily, not dragged there.

evidenceCatalog.name: Propped Stairwell Door
evidenceCatalog.description: The stairwell door was wedged open, against its own automatic closer.
evidenceCatalog.innocentExplanation: I propped it open when I came in. The lock sticks. It is an old building. I have done that in every dockside building I have worked in. It is not evidence of anything.
evidenceCatalog.trueSequenceOfEvents: Joel propped the door open on arrival as a practical habit. This detail is innocent in itself but creates opportunity — the open door is how Hollis followed Joel into the stairwell for the final confrontation. Without the propped door, Hollis might not have pursued Joel into the stairwell.

evidenceCatalog.name: Forearm Bruise
evidenceCatalog.description: A bruise on his forearm the medical examiner says the fall can't explain.
evidenceCatalog.innocentExplanation: I did not grab him. I did not touch him. Maybe he hit the railing when he fell. Maybe he bumped into something earlier. I was not the only person in that building.
evidenceCatalog.trueSequenceOfEvents: When Joel shoved Hollis on the stairwell landing, Hollis instinctively grabbed the railing with his right arm. The bruise was caused by the impact of his forearm against the metal railing as his grip failed and he went over. This is the most direct physical evidence of the shove, but Joel's explanation — that it could have come from the fall itself — is superficially plausible.

timeline.what: Nadia badges in at the main entrance and goes to her third-floor office.
Joel enters using a guest pass issued by Hollis. He goes to Hollis's second-floor office. He props the stairwell door open with a fire extinguisher on his way up.
Joel and Hollis discuss the fleet coordinator position. The conversation is tense. Joel knocks over Hollis's chair during a heated exchange. No physical contact occurs.
Nadia goes to the rooftop to smoke. She steps through standing water near the drainage grate, leaving wet boot prints when she returns to the third floor.

Nadia comes down from the rooftop. She hears raised voices and furniture scraping from the second floor. She sees the propped-open door but does not look inside. She continues down and exits the stairwell at the ground floor.

Joel leaves Hollis's office. Hollis follows him into the stairwell, still pressing the job offer. Joel turns and shoves Hollis. Hollis hits the railing, his forearm bruises on impact, and he falls two stories. Joel hears the impact. He stands on the landing for thirty seconds, then walks down and leaves without checking on Hollis.
A maintenance worker discovers Hollis's body at the base of the service stairwell. Emergency services are called.

locations.suspect-nadia-soren: Third-floor office (arrived 10:52 PM, working on project files)
Third-floor office (claims she was working the entire time)
locations.suspect-joel-maret: Second-floor office with Hollis (confirmed by both)

locations.suspect-nadia-soren: Claims she was finishing up on the third floor and left at 12:30 AM. Does not mention the rooftop or passing the second floor.
locations.suspect-joel-maret: Claims he was still in Hollis's office until approximately 1:00 AM, then left directly. Hollis was alive at his desk when Joel walked out.
